message.content:
In this repository, find every distinct server-side location that enforces memo visibility (i.e., controls who is allowed to view/read a "memo" resource). This could include things like:
- REST/GraphQL API route handlers or controllers that check visibility/permissions before returning a memo
- Middleware or authorization/policy classes that gate memo access
- Database query filters (e.g., WHERE clauses scoping visibility) used when fetching memos
- Service/model layer methods that check visibility before returning data
- GraphQL resolvers or field-level authorization for memo fields

Search the codebase thoroughly (grep for "memo", "visibility", "Memo" across the repo, look at models, controllers, services, policies, resolvers, middleware). List every distinct enforcement site you find with exact file paths and line numbers, plus a short quote/snippet of the relevant check. There should be at least three distinct sites - find all of them. Report back concisely with file:line and a one-line description of what each site does.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Server-side memo visibility enforcement sites (usememos/memos, Go backend)

**Core reusable check**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68` — `checkMemoReadAccess(ctx, memo)`: central helper; archived memos visible only to creator, non-public memos require auth, private memos require `creator_id == user.id`. Called from:
  - `memo_service.go:356` (`GetMemo`)
  - `memo_service.go:367` (`GetMemo`, for parent memo of a comment)
  - `memo_service_comments.go:148` (`ListMemoComments`)

**List/query-level filtering (service layer building `store.FindMemo`)**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227` — `ListMemos`: anonymous callers get `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`; authenticated callers get a CEL filter `creator_id == %d || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]` (or `VisibilityList=[PUBLIC,PROTECTED]` when listing another user's memos).
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:107-112` — `ListMemoRelations`: builds the same kind of CEL visibility filter (`visibility == "PUBLIC"` for anonymous, else `creator_id == %d || visibility in [...]`) passed to `store.FindMemoRelation.MemoFilter`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:156-159+` — `ListMemoComments`: same CEL filter pattern for listing comments.

**Explicit per-operation visibility checks (duplicated logic, not via the shared helper)**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:29-40` — `ListMemoReactions`: private memo requires creator/superuser; non-public requires auth.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:82-85` — `UpsertMemoReaction`: private memo requires creator/superuser before allowing a reaction.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:33-40` — `CreateMemoComment`: private memo requires creator/superuser before allowing a comment.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:43-44, 92-93, 133-134` — `CreateMemoShare`/`ListMemoShares`/`DeleteMemoShare`: require `creator_id == user.id || isSuperUser` to manage share links (access-control on the share feature itself, not content visibility, but gates who can create/view/revoke access).

**Database WHERE-clause enforcement (store layer, per DB backend)**
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:96-102` — builds `` `memo`.`visibility` IN (?,?...) `` from `find.VisibilityList`.
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go:89-95` — same, `memo.visibility in (...)`.
- `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go:104-110` — same, `` `memo`.`visibility` in (...) ``.
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:80-85` — compiles the CEL `MemoFilter` (visibility expression) into a SQL statement for the related-memo filter (mirrored in postgres/mysql `memo_relation.go`).

**Real-time delivery filtering**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-144` — `SSEClient.canReceive`: filters live SSE broadcast events by visibility — private events only delivered to the memo's creator or an admin; public/protected delivered to everyone (used by `Broadcast` at `sse_hub.go:115-132`).

**Feed-level filtering**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:88-94` (site feed) and `rss.go:138-145` (per-user feed) — RSS endpoints hard-code `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}`, so only public memos ever appear in RSS output.

**Coarse instance-level gate (related but not visibility-specific)**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/authz.go:58-67` — `Authorizer.CheckAccess`: method-level (not per-memo) gate deciding whether an anonymous caller may invoke a given RPC procedure at all (e.g. blocks anonymous `ListMemos`/`GetMemo` entirely on a private instance); this runs before any of the per-memo checks above and is shared by both Connect and gRPC-Gateway transports.

Note: this is a Go/Connect-RPC (gRPC-Gateway) backend, not GraphQL, so there are no GraphQL resolvers — the closest analog is the per-RPC-method authorization in `memo_service.go`/`reaction_service.go`/`memo_relation_service.go` plus the shared `Authorizer` interceptor.
